reply:
No. HttpOnly is a cookie attribute—it doesn't protect localStorage. Script can still read localStorage even if HttpOnly is set on your cookies.

If your JWT is in localStorage and sent as a bearer header (as you described), any XSS can grab it. An attacker doesn't need to break HttpOnly; HttpOnly doesn't apply to localStorage at all.

If you switched to storing the JWT in an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookie instead, then script cannot read it. XSS can't exfiltrate it. You'd trade the XSS risk for CSRF risk, which you'd handle with token validation or SameSite=Strict.

Cost of the current setup: XSS anywhere on your site (third-party script, dependency, DOM-based injection) steals the token and impersonates your user indefinitely.
